findings.title: No implementable acquisition path for authorizationRef/operationRef; security §7.1 inverts accepted v9 request semantics; SDK has no effect API

sources.selector: $.onTheWire (effectRequest names effect class token and authorizationRef; courier only); descriptorLayout fd0-fd4; closed hello/helloAck/select/selectAck bodies
effectRequest.body.authorizationRef/operationRef maxLength 1024, additionalProperties false

PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED meaning/scopeParameter; 'A request naming a denied token, an unknown token, or a scope wider than the grant is refused'; PT-ENV-READ meaning; FX-3 'host's declared structural allowlist'
§5.4 locator gj:<base64url(projectKey)>:<grantGeneration>:<seq>; §7.1 'authorizationRef names the GRANT record ... the request carries nothing else'
§8 ProviderSession interface (no effect operation); §6 'fixed argument vector and cleaned environment'
callbacks lifecycle_project_binding / lifecycle_project_root_verified (key is host-issued; a caller supplying a key never acquires a namespace; never a path segment)
'Components use host brokers'

findings.claim: A component must send a host-private journal locator it has no channel to learn and that cannot exist before the request whose acceptance the journal records; the locator embeds projectKey bytes; the SDK exposes no effect request.
findings.requiredDecision: Choose the accepted v9 request shape (token + bounded scope, host maps to grant) or a host-issued opaque per-spawn grant handle; deliver operationRef (and any handle) through the host-constructed environment under a declared structural variable, since one select per child makes one spawn one operation; keep the gj: locator host-internal; add ProviderSession.requestEffect; re-freeze control-completion (v6) with at-bound/over-bound cases for any changed field; extend FX-3 with the structural variable.
findings.challengeToLeadProposal: A 2048-byte authorizationRef cap admits the 1406-byte worst case but keeps projectKey on the wire, which no accepted contract requires or permits and the lifecycle contract's key-custody rules contradict. Bootstrap delivery is lawful only via the host-constructed environment; hello/helloAck/selectAck members, a new message type, a sixth descriptor, argv, or a provider-wire field each reopen DR-102 (SATISFIED) or the frozen provider wire.
findings.relationToInProgress: Not among the named repairs; the lead raised it mid-audit and it is confirmed here from bytes.

findings.title: Linux runtime attestation requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN (setns) and root-only TCG2 log reads; no privilege model decided

sources.selector: filesystemMeasurementTarget.linux.observerProcess/namespace/source (helper enters namespace with setns(nsfd, CLONE_NEWNS); setns failure refuses); resolutionPredicate.order[0]; measuredBootBind / fromBootLockdown (TCG2 event log)
§3.3 'At launch: ... plus the DR-126 resolution predicate'
§6.4 OUT_OF_ROOT_READ list 'the mount table via the v48 setns helper'; §8.4 runner requirements

findings.claim: setns(2) with CLONE_NEWNS needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the owning user namespace even for the caller's own mount namespace; /sys/kernel/security/tpm0/binary_bios_measurements is root-readable only; an unprivileged host refuses on every launch.
findings.requiredDecision: Decide the privilege model (none of setuid helper, root requirement, privileged daemon, or qualification-only observation is chosen) or supersede the setns mountinfo interface with an unprivileged read that retains the ns inode as identity.
findings.relationToInProgress: Distinct from SEC2-M1: the stock-OS baseline may drop measured boot but does not touch filesystemMeasurementTarget.linux; v3 must decide this explicitly.

findings.title: macOS codesign attestation helper contradicts 'framework absent' profiles and sits in the launch path; v49 acquisition interfaces unverified on VMs

sources.selector: platformAttestationOperation.macosCodesign (SecCodeCheckValidity, SecCodeCopySigningInformation); sameMeans/drift runtime resolution
§2 'core links libSystem only'; 'Required TCB verification helpers are separate processes with their own signed closure'; G02 'Include every mandatory core path'
§8.2 'the qualification verifier (a separate process) may use Security.framework'
§8.3 'framework, certificate store, font, ICU absent with inapplicability proofs'; v49 acquisition via bputil -d / system_profiler

findings.claim: A runtime loader attestation on macOS needs Security.framework in a mandatory closure member, so the framework class cannot be absent; alternatively the attestation is qualification-only and v48's runtime drift refusal is unimplemented on macOS.
findings.requiredDecision: State whether the helper runs at launch (then declare its Security.framework member and count its closure in G02) or only at qualification (then amend the runtime drift claim); measure bputil -d inside the D-102 hosted VM class before the v49 scheme is adopted.
findings.relationToInProgress: v49 is specified, not adopted; the contradiction is in v2 §8.2/§8.3 versus distribution §2 and v48, not in the v3 Linux repair.
